person.name: Dong Hwi Kim
person.affiliation: Mechanical Engineering & Electrical and Computer Engineering · Seoul National University
person.intro: I am an undergraduate at Seoul National University studying Mechanical Engineering and Electrical and Computer Engineering. My interests span 3D vision and perception, control, robotics, and autonomous driving.
person.bio: At the RPM Robotics Lab, I work with Prof. Ayoung Kim on 3D Gaussian Splatting for SLAM and 3D mapping. At the AIDAS Lab, my collaboration with Prof. Jaeyoung Do focuses on visual data augmentation for robot learning using reconstructed scenes and robot kinematics.

research.title: 3D Gaussian Splatting for SLAM
research.image_alt: Conceptual illustration of camera observations, Gaussian scene representation, and camera trajectory; not an experimental result

research.role: Research on 3D Gaussian Splatting-based SLAM at RPM Robotics Lab.

sections.heading: Gaussian scene mapping
sections.body: Investigating 3D Gaussian Splatting for SLAM and geometrically consistent mapping.

research.hero_caption: Conceptual illustration; method details and results are unpublished.
research.contribution_summary: Undergraduate research with Prof. Ayoung Kim at RPM Robotics Lab, Seoul National University.

research.title: 3D Gaussian Splatting for Robot Demonstration Augmentation
research.image_alt: An FR3 manipulation episode rendered from three camera viewpoints using Gaussian scene assets
research.summary: Render multi-view robot demonstrations from reconstructed scenes and robot kinematics.
research.role: Responsible for the 3DGS data augmentation module within a larger collaborative dataset project.

sections.heading: Scene alignment
sections.body: Align the reconstructed workcell with the robot and calibrated cameras before replaying motion.

points.text: Compare rigid-part distances with the robot URDF and ChArUco calibration.
Hold scale fixed and apply ICP to high-opacity Gaussian cores.
Check scene and robot dimensions in the same coordinate frame.

figure.alt: Repository figure comparing robot length-ruler errors and Gaussian-core distances before and after scale correction
figure.caption: Rigid-part distances check metric scale. Measurements refer to the repository’s reference capture.

sections.heading: Reusable robot-link assets
sections.body: Separate the captured robot into articulated link assets.

points.text: Assign each Gaussian to the nearest CAD link.
Apply inverse forward kinematics at the capture pose.
Reapply the captured pose and compare it with the original geometry.

sections.heading: Demonstration replay
sections.body: Replay a demonstration through the link assets. Render each camera from the same episode state.

points.text: Forward kinematics updates each link along the recorded trajectory.
Attachment and release rules update grasped objects.
Move the wrist camera with the robot and retain calibrated standing views.

figure.alt: Four rendered stages of the same FR3 cube-stacking episode
figure.caption: Approach, grasp, and stacking in a rendered episode. The montage illustrates kinematic replay.

sections.heading: Incomplete-surface repair
sections.body: Repair missing geometry before generating the augmented episodes.

points.text: Merge missing cube faces from a separately reconstructed rolled capture.
Replace reconstruction haze with a calibrated plane bounded by the measured table footprint.

sections.heading: Episode validation
sections.body: Check each generated episode before export.

points.text: Check metric scale, forward-kinematics round trips, grasp spacing, and object-pose continuity.
Reject black frames and check carried-object visibility in the wrist view.
Assess downstream robot learning separately from rendering and geometry checks.

research.card_role: Developing the 3DGS augmentation module in a larger dataset collaboration.
research.hero_caption: One rendered manipulation episode from three calibrated viewpoints.
research.result_summary: Working generation and validation module; broader dataset collaboration and downstream policy evaluation are ongoing.
research.contribution_summary: I develop the 3DGS augmentation module within a larger dataset collaboration at AIDAS Lab. My work covers reconstruction, alignment, rendering, and validation, building on RoboSplat and SplatSim.
research.overview: Turn workcell captures into reusable robot-learning assets. Replay a demonstration and render it from calibrated viewpoints.
result_notes: The broader dataset project is ongoing. Robot-policy performance has not yet been established by these generation checks.
research.motivation: Recorded demonstrations capture a task from a fixed set of cameras. A reconstructed scene lets us replay robot motion and render additional viewpoints.

motivation_points.text: Build reusable scene assets for visual data augmentation in robot learning.
Keep robot motion, object poses, and camera geometry consistent across views.

research.result_intro: The module generates rendered manipulation episodes and checks their geometry and visibility.

projects.title: Autonomous Object-Collecting Robot
projects.image_alt: Team 7's autonomous mecanum-wheel robot in the competition arena
projects.summary: An autonomous robot that detects, collects, and delivers objects within a three-minute match.
projects.role: Contributed across perception and model training, planning, data collection, hardware, and system integration with Team 7.

sections.heading: Hardware and motor interface
sections.body: A Jetson Orin Nano runs perception and navigation. An ESP32 drives the four mecanum-wheel motors.

points.text: Send body-frame motion commands over USB serial and convert them into wheel motion.
Calibrate wheel direction and feed-forward gains. Include a duration and auto-stop in motion commands.

sections.heading: Dual-camera perception
sections.body: Run YOLO instance segmentation on both cameras and combine the detections for navigation.

points.text: Use camera intrinsics and toe angles to express detections in a common forward-facing view.
Combine confidence, range-normalized mask area, bearing, and arena-cell ownership.
Send the merged detections through a UDP interface.

sections.formula: normalized area = mask area × (range / reference range)²

sections.heading: Collection and delivery planning
sections.body: Follow a fixed sweep route and use live detections to trigger object collection.

points.text: Approach a selected target with forward motion to load the passive basket.
Interrupt the sweep when the basket is full and return to the delivery zone.
Account for object retention during alignment, braking, and return maneuvers.

figure.alt: Official team repository diagram showing the object grid, storage corner, and robot start corner
figure.caption: Arena layout. The route links target collection to the delivery zone.

sections.heading: Localization and motion control
sections.body: Fit arena walls in LiDAR scans to estimate pose. Use integrated IMU yaw to stop calibrated turn pulses.

points.text: Use LiDAR feedback for strafing after the timed alternative proved unreliable during calibration.
Apply calibrated reverse pulses and keep cruise speed within the measured braking range.

sections.heading: On-device and field validation
sections.body: Tune perception and motion together on the competition hardware.

points.text: Benchmark models on the Jetson and set detection gates for the available observation window.
Check frozen streams and compare raw frames with motion logs during tuning.

projects.title: Accelerated MRI Reconstruction
projects.image_alt: Team MRI reconstruction framework using brain and knee experts with Feature VarNet and FI VarNet
projects.summary: Reconstruct brain and knee MRI images from undersampled multi-coil frequency measurements.

sections.heading: Reconstruction with data consistency
sections.body: Use Feature VarNet and FI VarNet to alternate learned reconstruction updates with the MRI measurement model.

points.text: Estimate sensitivity maps from the multi-coil measurements.
Refine feature representations with Feature VarNet and include image-domain cascades in FI VarNet.
Connect each update to the acquired k-space samples through the MRI encoding model.

sections.heading: Anatomy- and acceleration-specific models
sections.body: Train separate experts for each acquisition condition and select them with explicit inference rules.

points.text: Identify brain or knee inputs from coil count under the challenge data conventions.
Read the sampling mask to choose the 4× or 8× expert.

sections.heading: MRI-aware training
sections.body: Train with acquisition-aware augmentation, AdamW, and warmup followed by cosine scheduling.

points.text: Apply small rotations, shearing, and horizontal flips. Increase their strength during training.
Use DeepSpeed and activation checkpointing for the reconstruction networks.
Resume interrupted runs and convert distributed checkpoints into inference weights.

sections.heading: Weight averaging and output ensembling
sections.body: Combine compatible checkpoints and complementary reconstruction models.

points.text: Average model parameters into one checkpoint without adding inference passes.
Average reconstructed images from configured Feature VarNet and FI VarNet pairs.

projects.thumbnail_alt: Official poster for the fifth SNU FastMRI Challenge in 2025
projects.result_summary: 3rd place, 2025 SNU FastMRI Challenge; KRW 2,500,000 team prize.
projects.contribution_summary: I worked on Fourier-domain modeling with Jinseok Choi in Team 2rm1000. The model pipeline and competition submission were team work.
projects.overview: Recover brain and knee MRI images from undersampled multi-coil k-space. K-space contains the frequency-domain measurements. The challenge uses 4× and 8× acceleration.
projects.motivation: Acquiring fewer k-space samples accelerates MRI scans but leaves incomplete measurements. The task is to reconstruct an image while respecting the samples that were acquired.

motivation_points.text: Multi-coil k-space data with 4× or 8× acceleration.

projects.title: Multimodal Scene Reordering
projects.image_alt: Diagram of mapping frame-order views into a common coordinate system for Random4 inference
projects.summary: Recover the chronological order of four shuffled images using a vision-language model.

sections.heading: Vision-language model adaptation
sections.body: Adapt Qwen3.5-27B with LoRA and structured readouts for temporal ordering.

points.text: Six readouts compare the temporal order of image pairs.
Four readouts score chronological positions.
Use temporal-gap supervision and hard-negative ranking in the final training stage.

sections.heading: Constrained permutation decoding
sections.body: Combine pairwise and position evidence to score all 24 valid image orderings.

points.text: Choose the highest-scoring permutation so every image appears once.
Convert the ordered image sequence into per-input ranks using the inverse permutation.

sections.heading: Aggregation across input orderings
sections.body: Evaluate four image arrangements to reduce sensitivity to presentation order.

points.text: Map each arrangement’s logits back to the original image identities.
Average the aligned logits and decode the combined evidence.
Test the permutation mappings and final submission format.

sections.heading: Snapshot averaging
sections.body: Average nine language-LoRA snapshots from one training trajectory in CPU float32.

points.text: Merge the snapshots into one adapter without extra model passes.
The four input-order evaluations remain part of the final pipeline.

motivation_points.text: Use each image exactly once in the predicted sequence.
Align predictions from different image arrangements before combining them.

projects.title: Physics-Guided Wind Power Forecasting
projects.image_alt: Zephyr Analytics team cover for the 2025 Wind Power Prediction Competition
projects.summary: Forecast hourly wind generation by correcting a physical power curve with learned residuals.
projects.role: Model architecture design and hyperparameter optimization.

sections.heading: Physical baseline
sections.body: Estimate generation from weather conditions and the turbine power curve.

points.text: Include air-density estimates, using the Arden–Buck equation in feature construction.
Use the power curve as the initial forecast before learning a correction.

sections.heading: Residual learning
sections.body: Train LightGBM to predict the difference between observed generation and the physical baseline.

points.text: Subtract the baseline forecast from the observed generation.
Add the learned correction back to the physical estimate.

sections.formula: hybrid forecast = physical baseline + learned residual

sections.heading: Ensemble and hyperparameter optimization
sections.body: Combine the hybrid model with Ridge Regression and Random Forest forecasts.

points.text: Use Optuna to tune model hyperparameters and ensemble weights.
Inspect site-wise generation distributions alongside NMAE and settlement revenue.

projects.credit: Cover, architecture, and evaluation images are from the original Zephyr Analytics team presentation, supplied by Dong Hwi Kim.
projects.card_role: Model architecture design and hyperparameter optimization.
projects.hero_caption: Forecast architecture from the team presentation.
projects.hero_alt: Original team architecture diagram showing the physical power curve, residual correction, ensemble, and Optuna optimization
projects.result_summary: 3rd among 270 teams; reported NMAE 19.34% and settlement revenue rate 22.09% under the competition rule.
projects.contribution_summary: I designed the model architecture and optimized hyperparameters in Team Zephyr Analytics.
projects.overview: Forecast hourly generation for Gyeongju, Yangyang, and Yeongdeok. Evaluate both prediction error and settlement revenue.

result_figures.alt: Original team evaluation slide with NMAE, settlement revenue rate, and wind-farm distributions
result_figures.caption: Team-reported error and settlement results. The plots show site-wise generation distributions.

result_notes: Metrics follow the competition’s evaluation rule.
projects.motivation: A turbine power curve gives a physical estimate of wind generation. The model learns the error that remains between this estimate and observed production.

motivation_points.text: Predict hourly generation for Gyeongju, Yangyang, and Yeongdeok.
Measure forecast error and settlement revenue under the competition rules.

projects.title: Automated Filming Device
projects.image_alt: Sunflower-inspired face-tracking camera device with a yellow phone mount and white circular base
projects.summary: A Raspberry Pi camera mount with automatic face tracking and infrared remote control.

sections.heading: Hardware
sections.body: A Raspberry Pi connects the camera, two servos, and infrared receiver.

points.text: Rotate the camera horizontally and vertically with separate servo axes.
Use a ball-transfer unit to distribute weight and reduce friction.

figure.alt: Exploded hardware diagram of the pan–tilt filming device
figure.caption: Camera mount, two servo axes, and ball-transfer support.

sections.heading: Face tracking and servo control
sections.body: Read frames with Picamera2. Detect faces with OpenCV’s Haar cascade and track the largest face.

points.text: Normalize the face center’s horizontal and vertical offsets from the image center.
Convert these errors into incremental pan and tilt commands. The final implementation uses proportional feedback with zero derivative gain.
Clamp the requested angles and convert them into calibrated pigpio pulse widths.

figure.alt: Team diagram of the filming device software and control flow
figure.caption: Team software design. The controller description here follows the final implementation.

sections.heading: Remote control and device state
sections.body: Read LIRC remote commands in a separate thread while face tracking runs.

points.text: Switch between automatic tracking and manual operation.
Move either servo axis, stop motion, or exit.
Indicate face detection with an LED. Stop the camera and disable servo pulses on exit.

projects.title: TaXer and WaXer: Time-Series Forecasting
projects.image_alt: Original presentation slide showing the TaXer periodic feature extraction and cross-attention architecture
projects.summary: Combine a transformer forecaster with periodic or dilated-convolution temporal features.

sections.heading: TaXer: period-aware features
sections.body: Use TimesNet-style FFT analysis to identify dominant periods in the input sequence.

points.text: Reshape the sequence according to each selected period.
Apply 2D convolution to capture variation within and across periods.

sections.heading: Transformer integration
sections.body: Project the extracted temporal features into the transformer embedding dimension.

points.text: Create variable-wise patch embeddings and a global token.
Broadcast the projected temporal context across variables.
Let the sequence representation query this temporal context.
Produce predictions and restore each variable’s original scale.

sections.formula: temporal features → linear projection → cross-attention context

sections.heading: WaXer: convolutional alternative
sections.body: Replace the periodic extractor with WaveNet-style dilated causal convolutions.

points.text: Retain the projection and transformer integration pattern.
Evaluate forecast error and model size for the alternative temporal prior.

projects.hero_caption: Hybrid forecasting architecture from the team presentation.
projects.result_summary: Course-project Sticker Sales MSE: TaXer 0.1569, TimeXer 0.1647; additional weather and model-size comparisons in the report.
projects.contribution_summary: Team project with Jinwoo Seo, Hyeonseop Shin, and Manyoung Han. The architectures and reported experiments were developed by the team.
projects.overview: Test temporal feature extractors inside a transformer forecaster. Compare periodic and convolutional representations on weather and sales data.
result_notes: The report also compares weather forecasts and model sizes under the project’s experimental setup.

result_figures.alt: Team presentation comparing ground-truth and predicted time-series traces
result_figures.caption: Ground-truth and predicted sequences from the team presentation.

projects.motivation: Temporal feature extractors encode different assumptions about a sequence. This course project compares periodic and convolutional features within a transformer forecasting pipeline.

motivation_points.text: Use FFT-selected periods and two-dimensional convolution.
Use dilated causal convolutions as an alternative temporal prior.

projects.result_intro: Sticker Sales results from the course-project report. Lower MSE is better.
